title: A spiritual director
hookLine: a guide who listens and helps you discern
tomorrow: why would anyone choose to stay a little hungry?

lines: SAMUEL RUNS TO THE WRONG VOICE.
SPEAK, LORD, FOR THY SERVANT HEARETH.
cards: Athletes have coaches who watch film with them. Writers have editors. When you can't tell God's voice from your own, who do you ask?
The boy Samuel had the same trouble. Asleep in the temple, he hears his name, and runs to the old priest Eli: here I am. Eli sends him back to bed.
It happens again, and then, the text says, a third time. Then Eli realizes who's calling, and gives him one line to answer with: "Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth."

teach.b: Eli didn't hear God for Samuel. He helped Samuel hear. Catholics call that kind of help spiritual direction: someone who listens to your prayer and your life and helps you notice where God is moving.
Do you need one? Two Catholic saints lean different ways.
Francis de Sales, writing to a reader he calls Philothea, says plainly: if you want to grow in devotion, find a good guide, and pray to find one. Don't walk the road alone.
John of the Cross agrees a guide can help, but warns hard: the main guide of a soul is the Holy Spirit, and a director who doesn't understand prayer can do real damage.
Better a careful search than the first person available. Both are saints, and both sides have a point. Here's what they share.
Neither treats a director as someone who tells you what God wants. Both treat discernment as testing.
The first letter of John says it: "believe not every spirit, but try the spirits if they be of God."
One to tell a friend: the Catechism describes direction as a gift the Holy Spirit gives to certain of the faithful, so a director isn't always a priest.
Lay people and religious sisters do it too.

how: Catholics who want spiritual direction often ask their parish, a nearby retreat house or a campus ministry for a trained director, usually meeting about once a month to talk about prayer and life.

o: someone who listens and helps you discern God's voice
a choir leader who directs the music at Mass
a priest who assigns your penance after confession

games.q: who said what about guides — tap the pairs.
p: find a good guide, and pray to find one
the Holy Spirit is the main guide
try the spirits if they be of God

s: a spiritual director's job is to tell you what God wants
Eli didn't hear for Samuel; he helped him hear. a director helps you test, not obey.
only priests can be spiritual directors
the Catechism calls direction a gift given to certain of the faithful; lay people and sisters direct too.
John of the Cross warned that a director who doesn't understand prayer can do harm
he called the Holy Spirit the main guide, and urged care in choosing a human one.

games.q: your cousin says: 'a director? i'll just pray. the Holy Spirit is enough.' you lean that way too. what's the best case for Francis de Sales's side?
o: even Samuel needed Eli to say: that voice is God's; answer it.
a director tells you God's will, so you don't have to discern.
Church law requires every Catholic to have a director.
games.why: de Sales's case: we often can't tell God's voice from our own, and Samuel ran to the wrong voice until Eli helped. John of the Cross would add: choose that helper carefully.

practice: Close your eyes. If you pray, say Samuel's line silently: speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth. If not, let one quiet question rise instead: who listens to me well?
Notice whose face comes up. That person might be your Eli, or might know one.

wordCard.voice: A spiritual director. A guide who listens with you, helps you test what you hear, and never hears for you.

carryVoice: Your words for today: a guide, like Eli, who taught Samuel what to say instead of answering for him. That's day 1739.
